conventions.convention: QFT_N is the inverse of the negative-sign, N^(-1/2)-normalized DFT, so its basis kernel has positive exponent 2πixy/N. QFT_1 is the identity.
Wire order is q_(n-1), …, q_0, with integer x = Σ x_j 2^j. Targets are processed in descending j; each Hadamard precedes its lower-control phases; reversal swaps occur last.
The integer cutoff m is at least one; phases CP_s are omitted exactly when s > m. Hadamards and reversal swaps remain. If m ≥ n, truncation is exact.
Each ideal Hadamard, exact controlled phase, and named SWAP costs one gate. Expanding a SWAP replaces it with three exact CNOTs. Finite-set synthesis is counted separately.

Total variation is one half of the sum of absolute probability differences. Projective operator distance is infimum over unit scalars of ||U − λV||; measurement guarantees concern unit inputs and computational-basis output laws.

Finite-set compilation assumes a fixed certified inverse-closed dense SU(2) package, rational tolerances within its exact-real compiler range, and exact CNOTs. Scalar phases become metadata for the standalone circuit; no outer-controlled-QFT or classical bit-time guarantee is asserted.

load_bearing.statement: For n ≥ 0 and binary input x = Σ x_i2^i, set R_j = 2^(-1/2)(|0⟩ + exp(2πi Σ_(i=0)^j x_i2^(-(j-i+1)))|1⟩). In wire order q_(n-1), …, q_0, QFT_(2^n)|x⟩ is R_0 ⊗ … ⊗ R_(n-1); before final reversal the factors are R_(n-1) ⊗ … ⊗ R_0. The n = 0 case is the empty tensor 1.

For every n ≥ 0, the exact binary circuit implements the positive-sign QFT_(2^n) in the declared output order on every state. Reversing the gate list and taking adjoints gives the negative-sign inverse QFT with the same ideal gate count.

For nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces S,R with specified orthonormal bases and linear T:S→S, ||T ⊗ I_R|| = ||T||. Conjugating an endomorphism A by a unitary wire permutation P preserves its operator norm.

For n ≥ 1 and integers 1 ≤ m < n, ||QFT_(2^n) − QFT_(2^n)^(m)|| ≤ Σ_(s=m+1)^n (n−s+1)2π/2^s ≤ 2πn2^(-m). For m ≥ n the error is zero. For 0 < ε < 1, m = min{n, ceil(log_2(2πn/ε))} gives error at most ε.
For unitaries U,V on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space with fixed orthonormal computational basis, a unit input ψ, and ε ≥ 0, d_pr(U,V) ≤ ε implies d_TV(p_U^ψ,p_V^ψ) ≤ ε.
On two ordered qubit wires, S = C_12 C_21 C_12, where products act right to left. Thus a wire swap has an exact three-CNOT implementation without ancillas.
For n ≥ 0, the exact circuit uses n Hadamards, n(n−1)/2 controlled phases, floor(n/2) SWAPs, and no ancillas. Expanding the SWAPs replaces them with 3 floor(n/2) CNOTs.

concerns.concern: Proof 3.1 says, “P and P^{-1} preserve norms, so each has operator norm 1.” The permutation clause permits any finite ordered tensor register, and its cited tensor-register definition explicitly permits a zero-dimensional factor. On the resulting zero space both norms are 0 under the cited operator-norm definition. The conjugation equality remains true there, but the proof needs the immediate zero-space case or bounds by 1 instead of the asserted equalities.

seams_checked.note: Compilation preserves the certified base-net, inverse-closure, SU(2), rational-tolerance and exact-real hypotheses; it uses the word-length bound without claiming bit complexity or outer-controlled phase invariance.
Ket and coordinate uses respect the root linear-first pairing and the Dirac argument reversal.
Big-endian indices, lexicographic tensor order, factor permutations, and the empty register agree. The minor zero-space proof issue is recorded separately in concerns.
Controlled phases use the exact control-first diagonal matrix; CNOT orientations and inverse chronology agree. The compilation caveat respects the controlled relative-phase distinction.
The Hadamard matrix and its basis action retain the supplier's exact scalar phase.
Chronological lists denote right-to-left products of gates embedded on distinct ordered wires. Counts distinguish named gates, workspace and explicitly available operations.

The algorithm reverses and adjoints the positive-sign QFT, producing the negative kernel used in the outcome and superposition formulas. Its access-cost theorem quotes the exact ideal gate counts faithfully.

The finite-grid subgradient lemma uses the negative-sign inverse on power-of-two coordinate registers, consistently with its positive phase encoding. QFT gate costs remain separate from its value-query count.
